newsitem.title: USA: Study links asthma to menstrual cycle.
newsitem.headline: Study links asthma to menstrual cycle.

text.p: Women are more likely to suffer a severe asthma attack just before and during menstrual bleeding, apparently because of fluctuations in body hormones, researchers reported on Sunday.

The finding, based on a study of 182 women and conducted at the Medical College of Pennsylvania in Philadelphia, found that women were more than twice as likely to seek emergency room treatment for a severe asthma attack at the end of the menstrual cycle than at other times.
Huge fluctuations in levels of oestrogen hormones may be the culprit, said the study appearing in the Archives of Internal Medicine, a publication of the American Medical Association.

"We conclude that increased numbers of females (seeking treatment) at the emergency department may be a result of dynamic changes in hormone levels during the perimenstrual interval," the study said. Perimenstrual refers to the period three days before bleeding starts and the four days thereafter.
"As such, female sex may be a significant and independent risk factor for acute exacerbations of asthma," it added.

The report said very little is known about the effects of variations in sex steroids on asthma, a disease that afflicts 10 million people in the United States alone and is one of the most common reasons people seek emergency room treatment.
The researchers said the asthma attacks in women while more frequent during the time period involved are not generally any more severe than attacks suffered by women at other times during the cycle.
